title: Hootsuite Pricing 2026: Plans and Per-User Costs

body_markdown:
## Automating repetitive social work around Hootsuite with Activepieces


Some of the chores around Hootsuite can go to Activepieces, a separate workflow tool whose free plan costs $0 and allows unlimited flows.


It doesn't change what Hootsuite charges, so it earns a place only after you've priced your seats, accounts and add-ons against the plan and against Sprout Social.


Any hours it saves are a labor saving, not a discount on the invoice.


Check Hootsuite's own integrations first, because a connection that ships with the plan costs you nothing extra to set up.


### When a workflow tool helps and when it does not


Where a person is copying something from one place to another and adding no judgment, a workflow tool fits. The same work done by hand is also where an agency quietly absorbs cost.


The client never sees it. Agencies rarely bill the hour spent pasting approved copy into drafts, so the retainer carries it.


Chores a separate workflow tool could take:


- Copy approved posts from a content calendar into a draft
- Send weekly metrics to Slack
- Log published links to a sheet


Those three are the pattern: each starts from a trigger, moves a defined piece of data, and ends in a place someone already looks.


When the task needs a decision, a workflow tool helps less. Moderating a reply in the inbox, choosing which post to boost, or judging a crisis comment should stay with a person inside Hootsuite.


If a connection breaks and nobody notices, posts stall or reports go missing, and that failure lands on you rather than the client.


Adding a workflow tool means a second system to maintain. If Hootsuite already does the job natively, a separate tool is one more thing to own for no gain.


### An example: content calendar row to scheduled draft


Say you mark a row approved in the content calendar once the client signs off.


In Activepieces you'd build a flow that watches for that status change and reads the copy, date and account from the row, and each run of it is 1 credit however many steps it has, out of the 1,000 credits a month the free plan includes.


The flow then creates a draft in Hootsuite for a person to check and schedule.


Where Hootsuite's connection doesn't cover a step, you'd need to confirm what its API allows before you tell the client that step runs automatically.


The draft is the point. A person still reviews it, so the flow removes the retyping without removing the check.


Nobody on the agency side has to be a builder to get that flow. Describe the calendar-to-draft chore in Activepieces' built-in chat and it builds and publishes a real workflow you can read, version and approve.


Custom RBAC and audit logs come with Ultimate and Enterprise, not the free plan. Every run leaves a trace anyone on the team can read, so you can see exactly what it did to a client's draft.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties already run Activepieces in production.
